newsitem.title: FRANCE: Former Riviera boss on trial for sleaze.
newsitem.headline: Former Riviera boss on trial for sleaze.

text.p: A former Riviera political boss, who liked to call himself "the Godfather", went on trial on Monday accused of taking kickbacks in the latest political sleaze scandal in France.

Maurice Arreckx, 79, the southern Var department's representative to the French senate when arrested in August 1994, is accused of extorting 1.8 million francs ($350,000) in return for awarding a construction contract in Toulon.

"I am a man of private means," the former mayor of the Mediterranean port city told the court when asked his profession at the start of the trial, expected to last a week. Arreckx has been held in pre-trial detention for 288 days.

He is on trial with five other people in a case that could expose shadowy ties between politicians, companies and the underworld along the Cote d'Azur, where a series of politicians have been involved in corruption probes.
The Arreckx case has drawn special attention because of his reputed ties with local gangland chief Jean-Louis Fargette who has since been murdered.

Investigators have said that Fargette claimed that Arreckx "swindled" him out of a cut in the kickback money, which was alleged to have been paid by a unit of utilities group Cie Generale des Eaux in return for a contract to build a college for engineers in Toulon.

The Var has been under the spotlight since 1993 when local parliamentarian Yann Piat, like Arreckx a member of the centre-rightist Union for French Democracy (UDF) party, was killed after she threatened to reveal "Mafia-like" activities in the region.

Another top southern politician, Cannes mayor Michel Mouillot, is in detention on suspicion of extorting cash from a British casino. And mayors of Nice, Lyon and Grenoble have all been embroiled in political scandals.
